host_linked_starter.note: Host-linked to HAM AND to FSM, CRM, CPQ, SUB-MGMT, FIN. Content is HVAC field service (customers, crm_contacts, customer_sites, installed_equipment, service_pm_schedules, service_work_orders, field_visits, dispatch_records, service_contracts, sales_quotes, customer_invoices, spare_parts_inventory). NOT IT hardware. See boundary finding.

surface_matrix.compliance_basis: physical inventory verification / SOX asset existence
Certificate of Destruction / R2v3 / NAID AAA data-sanitization proof
NIST 800-88 media sanitization / GDPR Art.17 / chain-of-custody

missing.reason: Junction linking hardware_asset to a user/department; the single most-mastered HAM concept after the asset itself. Present in all 6 vendors (Snipe-IT asset->user, Asset Panda assignee, ServiceNow assigned_to). HAM currently has no way to record who holds an asset.
Physical/logical location master. Universal across vendors (Snipe-IT locations, Device42 buildings/rooms/racks, Asset Panda sites). Required to answer 'where is this asset'. Currently absent.

Physical inventory verification event (last-audited, audit due, scan result). Snipe-IT asset_maintenances/audits, Asset Panda audit, ServiceNow stocktake. Underpins SOX asset-existence assertion. Absent.

NIST 800-88 wipe/destruction record tied to a disposed asset. Non-optional compliance entity (GDPR Art.17 erasure proof, data-bearing-device handling). hardware_disposal_records exists but does not capture per-device sanitization method/verification.
ITAD chain-of-custody log from decommission through certified disposal (collected->transported->received->destroyed). Required for R2v3/NAID-grade disposal assurance. Absent.
Certificate of Destruction / recycling certificate issued by the ITAD vendor, attached to disposal record. Distinct from the disposal event itself. Compliance evidence artifact.

Repair/service event against an asset (consumes spare_parts_inventory, may invoke warranty). Snipe-IT asset_maintenances, EZOffice/AssetPanda maintenance. Closes the loop between warranties + spare parts. Absent.

Book/financial value over useful life per asset or model. Snipe-IT depreciations, Asset Panda/EZOffice depreciation, Device42. SOX/GAAP fixed-asset basis. Absent (note: cross-asset financial depreciation may belong to FIN; per-hardware-asset book value belongs here).
Manufacturer master normalizing hardware_models (Dell, HP, Cisco). Snipe-IT manufacturers, Device42, ServiceNow. Currently models have no manufacturer master.
Deployable/pending/archived/broken status taxonomy (Snipe-IT status_labels, ServiceNow asset state). Drives lifecycle. Currently no status master.
Category/type taxonomy (laptop, monitor, server). Snipe-IT categories, Asset Panda groups. Currently no category master.
Check-out/check-in transition log distinct from durable assignment (Snipe-IT checkout, EZOffice reservations/checkout, Asset Panda). Custody timeline. Absent.
Stockroom/storeroom master holding spare parts + pre-deployment assets (ServiceNow stockroom, EZOffice, Device42). spare_parts_inventory exists but has no stocking-location master. Common.
Sub-component master (RAM, disk, GPU) installed into a parent asset (Snipe-IT components, Device42 parts). Common for hardware-depth vendors.
Consumable stock (toner, cables) drawn down by assets (Snipe-IT consumables, EZOffice). Common, mid-market.

Procurement record sourcing assets (Snipe-IT, EZOffice, Asset Panda, ServiceNow). NOTE possible WRONG-OWNERSHIP: enterprise procurement may belong to a Procurement/PROC umbrella, not HAM. Flag for user, not an unconditional add.

scope_creep.reason: spare_parts_inventory is correctly mastered in HAM-WARRANTY-PARTS but ALSO appears as embedded_master in the HVAC starter (171). The HVAC instance is a field-service spare-parts concept, not IT hardware. This is a symptom of the mis-hosted starter, not HAM scope creep. Resolution is the host-link removal below, not a HAM change.

boundary_findings.finding: Module 171 is host-linked to HAM (domain_id=51) via domain_module_host_domains. Its 12 embedded_master entities (customers, crm_contacts, customer_sites, installed_equipment, service_pm_schedules, service_work_orders, field_visits, dispatch_records, service_contracts, sales_quotes, customer_invoices, spare_parts_inventory) describe an HVAC field-service business: scheduling technicians, dispatching field visits, servicing customer-owned installed equipment, quoting and invoicing customers. None of this is IT hardware asset management. installed_equipment's own description calls it 'Customer-owned equipment that the service organization installs and maintains ... the asset register that work orders are performed against' = a field-service asset register, NOT an IT hardware register.
boundary_findings.evidence: Module 171 is host-linked to 6 domains total: FSM (31), CRM (69), CPQ (73), SUB-MGMT (97), HAM (51), FIN (65). Its natural primary home is FSM (Field Service Management). The HAM link is the anomalous one. HVAC-SVC-MGMT is a small-org field-service starter that embeds CRM/CPQ/SUB-MGMT/FIN masters as embedded_master and should consume HAM only if it tracks the service org's OWN IT hardware, which it does not.
boundary_findings.recommendation: Remove the domain_module_host_domains row linking module 171 to domain 51 (HAM). DESTRUCTIVE (DELETE of a host-link row) -> requires explicit user approval; do NOT execute in this audit. Keep the FSM host link (primary) and the CRM/CPQ/SUB-MGMT/FIN consumer links as appropriate to that starter's design. This finding does NOT fold any HVAC entity into HAM's hardware surface.
boundary_findings.do_not: Do NOT add customers, installed_equipment, service_work_orders, field_visits, dispatch_records, service_pm_schedules, service_contracts, sales_quotes, customer_invoices, or crm_contacts to HAM. They are field-service / CRM / CPQ / billing concepts.

modularization.two_module_split_assessment: The HAM-ASSET-REGISTRY (identity/lifecycle/custody) vs HAM-WARRANTY-PARTS (warranty/disposal/spare-parts/maintenance) split is coherent and self-explaining for a first-time deployer; both modules retain >=1 master and the boundary (register vs post-deployment service/end-of-life) is clean. Rule #14 satisfied: 2 modules, each with masters, for a >=3-capability domain. The split is sound; the gap is depth, not structure. Compliance/disposal entities (data_sanitization_records, asset_chain_of_custody_events, asset_disposal_certificates) all land naturally in HAM-WARRANTY-PARTS; custody/audit/taxonomy entities land in HAM-ASSET-REGISTRY.

recommendations.reason: Two-module split is coherent. No merge/split/rename needed. Fill depth (custody, audit, sanitization compliance) within the existing two modules.
Remove the HAM host link on module 171 (see boundary_findings). Destructive; user approval required. This is the only modularization-class action for HAM and it lives outside HAM's own two modules.
